**In brief**

- The Government set out a three-year strategy to target the highest-harm threats, integrate financial intelligence and strengthen enforcement, as when Dan Jarvis, Minister of State (Home Office) (Security), said it is
"Backed by over £550m of investment over three years and resulting in an increase of 500 new law enforcement officers and specialists by end 2029."

The strategy sets out three objectives: firstly, to make the UK’s defences more effective and efficient, while making it simpler and safer for honest businesses to grow; secondly, to disrupt money laundering and dismantle high-harm criminal networks at home and abroad; and finally, to recover more criminal assets for law enforcement, victims and the public.

cited.cited_text: Second, we will integrate financial intelligence and deepen collaboration between government, law enforcement and the private sector to identify criminal networks earlier and support faster disruption and asset recovery. We will establish a new National Financial Intelligence Service within the National Crime Agency’s National Economic Crime Centre, bringing together public and private sector intelligence to identify criminal networks earlier and support faster disruption and asset recovery. We will strengthen the UK Financial Intelligence Unit, including through building a new Suspicious Activity Reports Digital Service, and by improving access to and usage of financial intelligence across policing. We will also deepen international partnerships against shared illicit finance risks, piloting a multinational public-private information-sharing partnership and improving cooperation to trace, restrain and recover assets held overseas.

We will expand the Asset Management Office to support all agencies with powers to recover assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002. markdown:
**In brief**

- The Government set out a three-year strategy to target the highest-harm threats, integrate financial intelligence and strengthen enforcement, as when Dan Jarvis, Minister of State (Home Office) (Security), said it is "Backed by over £550m of investment over three years and resulting in an increase of 500 new law enforcement officers and specialists by end 2029." [Source 1]
- Ministers framed money laundering as a threat to security and communities, as when Dan Jarvis said it "fuels drug trafficking, people smuggling, fraud and corruption" [Source 1] and can enable terrorism and hostile state activity.
- The strategy sets recovering criminal assets as a separate objective, as when Dan Jarvis said it aims "to recover more criminal assets for law enforcement, victims and the public." [Source 1]

**Home Office ministers – setting out a strategy**

Dan Jarvis, Minister of State (Home Office) (Security), presented the strategy as a coordinated response, saying "a coordinated and intelligence-led response is required." [Source 1] His written statement of 15 September 2026 described the strategy's main measures:

- On targeting, he said "We will intensify enforcement against criminal fronts, strengthen controls on Post Office cash deposits, and reform anti-money laundering supervision" [Source 1]. He also said the Government would "consult on changes to reduce low-value compliance and reporting activity" [Source 1].
- On intelligence, he said "We will establish a new National Financial Intelligence Service within the National Crime Agency's National Economic Crime Centre" [Source 1]. He also announced a new Suspicious Activity Reports Digital Service.
- On capability and asset recovery, he said "We will expand the Asset Management Office to support all agencies with powers to recover assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002" [Source 1]. He also promised investment in "financial investigators, forensic accountants and cryptoasset capabilities." [Source 1]

About the evidence: The only relevant record is one written statement from a Home Office minister, dated 15 September 2026, so no other ministers' views, opposition responses, debates or votes are covered. The other records supplied (on the criminal justice system, a 2012 capital gains tax answer, Scotland and the Bank of England, and Northern Ireland security) do not address money laundering or asset recovery and are not used.
